title: Stablecoin Atlas
intro: Who issues stablecoins, which chains they settle on, the APIs that make them usable, and the networks and institutions bringing them to users.
cardIntro: Issuers, settlement chains, on/off-ramps and orchestration APIs, card networks, and the banks and apps putting stablecoins in front of users.
initiativesHeading: How the world’s largest companies are using stablecoins

layers.name: Issuers & reserves
layers.description: The companies that mint stablecoins and hold the assets backing them. Revenue mostly comes from interest on reserves, which is why distribution deals and yield-sharing shape this layer.
watch: Reserve composition and attestation cadence
Licensing: EMI status under MiCA, permitted-issuer status under the GENIUS Act
Revenue-sharing deals with distributors such as exchanges, wallets and PSPs
Multi-chain support and native cross-chain transfer

layers.name: Chains & settlement
layers.description: The blockchains and interoperability protocols that tokens move on. General-purpose chains still carry most volume, while payments-specific chains compete on fees, finality and compliance features.
watch: Where stablecoin supply and transfer volume actually sit
Payments chains launched by Stripe, Circle and Tether-aligned teams
Gas abstraction, fee tokens and finality times
Bridging and native cross-chain transfer standards

layers.name: Infrastructure & APIs
layers.description: The B2B layer that turns stablecoins into something a bank or fintech can integrate: on/off-ramps, orchestration, virtual accounts, custody, wallets and compliance.
watch: API surface: virtual accounts, payouts, issuance, wallets
KYC/KYB turnaround and coverage by country
Sandbox fidelity, webhooks, error models and versioning
Consolidation through acquisitions by networks and PSPs

layers.name: Networks & acquirers
layers.description: Card networks, acquirers and PSPs plugging stablecoins into existing merchant acceptance, settlement and payout flows, so neither merchant nor consumer has to touch a wallet.
watch: Stablecoin settlement for issuers and acquirers
Stablecoin-linked card issuing programmes
Merchant acceptance that settles in fiat
Which infrastructure providers they buy or partner with

layers.name: Front-end institutions
layers.description: The brands end users and businesses actually touch: neobanks, remittance apps, commerce platforms and banks. Most of them rent their stablecoin infrastructure, which makes this layer the customer base for the infra layer.
watch: Which infra provider powers each product
Remittance corridors moving to stablecoin rails
Bank deposit tokens and tokenised cash
Consumer yield and stablecoin balances in apps

layers.name: Regulation
layers.description: The regimes that decide who may issue stablecoins, how reserves are held, and who may distribute them. They directly shape partner onboarding requirements and KYC/KYB obligations.
watch: Implementing rules and licensing timelines
Treatment of yield and interest on stablecoins
Rules for foreign-issued coins and passporting
Travel rule and AML expectations for intermediaries
